solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Pep at fault and opposite number brilliant, drop off sharply (2,3,4,1,5)

blocks.note: your like is your counterpart or equal

annotation.surface: A deflated player turns on a brilliant rival, as if in a sports report.
annotation.walkthrough: The four chunks run in clue order; 'brilliant' reads as praise but is the literal 'on fire' sense. Only the last three words define.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to go out like a light is to fall asleep at once, which is dropping off sharply.

entries.clue: Despicable people bounding round delta with waders (7)

indicators.note: to bound something is to form its boundary, so GITS encloses the letters that follow

annotation.surface: Nasty types circle a river delta hunting birds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round' and 'delta' look like a river mouth being circled, but they are just O and D. A git is a British insult for an unpleasant person.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: godwits are long-billed wading birds, so they are waders.

entries.clue: Playing between flat and house? (2,5)

blocks.note: not children at play but actors performing
not two homes: a flat is a painted scenery panel and the house is the audience

annotation.surface: Someone seems to be playing in the street between an apartment and a house.
annotation.walkthrough: Flat and house read as homes, but in a theatre a flat is backstage scenery and the house is the auditorium; an actor performing stands between them.
annotation.definitionFit: Theatre jargon: the stage lies between the scenery flats and the house, so anyone playing there is on stage.

entries.clue: Cardinal nailed by two articles, say journalists (3,6,6)

indicators.note: a board nailed by two others is fixed between them, so FOUR sits between two THEs

annotation.surface: A cardinal pinned down by two articles in the papers, as the press would say.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is a counting number; 'articles' suggests newspaper pieces but means the grammatical THE.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for the press, named as a fourth power alongside the three old estates of the realm; journalists collectively make it up.

entries.clue: One put inside abbey opening late, extremely effusive (8)

indicators.note: late means dead and gone, so the abbey's opening letter no longer exists
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so take its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A body is laid inside an abbey that opens late, with a gushing tribute.
annotation.walkthrough: Tintern Abbey is a famous ruined abbey in Wales. 'Late' means deceased here, so its opening T has gone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: an internee is someone interned, confined in a camp or prison, i.e. put inside.

entries.clue: What’s chewed by cattle in Spain, note – and old rhino in Portugal! (6)

indicators.note: the cud sits in the letters for Spain and note, as food sits in a stomach

annotation.surface: A cheery note on cattle fodder in Spain and an elderly rhinoceros in Portugal.
annotation.walkthrough: CUD goes inside E + SO. Rhino is old British slang for money, so the 'animal' is a currency.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: rhino means money, and the escudo was Portugal's money before the euro, hence old.

entries.clue: Artistic type designed a Nordic divan for stars to sit on (8,2,5)

indicators.note: to design is to plan a new shape, so the letters take a new arrangement
in a down answer, what sits on something is placed above it

annotation.surface: A designer makes a Scandinavian sofa for celebrities to lounge on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stars' seems to be celebrities using the divan, but it is the constellation Leo placed on top of the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, understated: Leonardo was an artist, so the greatest of artistic types.

entries.clue: Seize grain and fruit (7)

blocks.note: gr is the written abbreviation of grain, the small unit of weight

annotation.surface: Grabbing cereal and fruit, as from a breakfast table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grain' reads as cereal beside 'fruit', but it is the unit of weight.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to grapple with someone is to seize and wrestle them.

entries.clue: I want to put aside a defective, still spinning washing machine … (4-3)

indicators.note: the A is put aside, set apart from the rest, so it is removed
something defective is not in working order, so the letters lose their order
a thing spinning turns round, so BUT turns round to TUB

blocks.clueFragment: I want to put aside a defective
blocks.note: I WANT minus A leaves IWNT, then rearranged

annotation.surface: A customer wants rid of a broken washer that won't stop spinning, and the ellipsis leads on to 15 down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' is the adverb meaning 'yet', i.e. BUT, not 'motionless'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a twin-tub is an old-style washing machine with separate wash and spin drums.

entries.clue: When ground patty oddly spiced, having indigestion (9)

indicators.note: ground up like meat, so the letters are broken down and reformed
read as 'in the odd positions', so take letters 1, 3 and 5

annotation.surface: Eating a minced patty with odd spices leaves someone with indigestion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like minced meat for the patty, but it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: dyspeptic means suffering from dyspepsia, the medical word for indigestion.

entries.clue: Reversing any minute now for person in Muscat? (5)

indicators.note: as a car reverses, the letters go backwards

annotation.surface: A driver about to reverse out any minute now, somewhere in Muscat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a mo' is British slang for 'in a moment'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Muscat is the capital of Oman, so a person there is probably an Omani, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: One of 50 fooled when overthrown ball goes past infielder’s head (5)

indicators.note: something overthrown is turned upside down, so HAD is turned round
a ball that goes past a fielder ends up beyond him, so O comes after the other pieces
the head of a word is its top, i.e. first, letter

annotation.surface: A baseball fielder is fooled when a wild throw sails past him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overthrown' is a fielding error in the surface but the reversal signal in the wordplay. The 50 are the US states.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by membership: the United States has 50 states and Idaho is one of them.

entries.clue: Where VIP may be seen looking embarrassed with wig (3,6)

blocks.note: a rug is slang for a wig, and a carpet is a big rug

annotation.surface: A celebrity blushes when spotted in a toupee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rug' is joke slang for a hairpiece; the setter stretches it to carpet.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: VIPs are welcomed along a red carpet, so that is where one may be seen.

entries.clue: Drinks slings, bored by goof (8)

indicators.note: a hole bored by a drill has the drill inside it, so ERR goes into SHIES

annotation.surface: A cocktail order: drinks and slings, with a bore of a fool nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drinks' and 'slings' both look like cocktails (a Singapore sling), but slings means throws.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: sherries are glasses of fortified Spanish wine, a kind of drink.

entries.clue: Perhaps once leaving mass, angry over losing face with bishop (6)

indicators.note: the mass leaves the word, so M walks out of MAD
the face is the front, so the first letter is lost

blocks.note: M, the letter removed from MAD

annotation.surface: Someone once stormed out of Mass furious with the bishop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mass' and 'bishop' dress a church scene but are just M and B.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: 'once' is itself an adverb, so 'perhaps once' points to the word class.

entries.clue: … and trace repair (8)

annotation.surface: Continuing 8 down: send the machine back and track down a repair.
annotation.walkthrough: The ellipsis only carries the surface on from 8 down. 'Repair' is the verb 'go somewhere', not 'mend'.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal sense: to repair to another room is to withdraw there.

entries.clue: Shrink from Lima – he is led by old Adler’s teachings first and foremost (6)

indicators.note: whatever leads walks in front, so OAT goes before HE
'first' and 'foremost' both point at the front letter of each word

annotation.surface: A psychiatrist from Lima follows the old doctrines of Alfred Adler, the Austrian psychologist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' tempts as a psychiatrist to go with Adler, but it is the verb 'recoil from'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to loathe something is to recoil or shrink from it in disgust.

entries.clue: Academician probing malign Canadian politician, maybe (7)

indicators.note: a probe is pushed inside something, so RA goes into LIBEL

annotation.surface: A scholar digs into a smear against a Canadian politician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Malign' looks like an adjective describing the politician, but it is the verb 'defame'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Liberals are one of Canada's main parties, so a Canadian politician may be a Liberal.

entries.clue: Defendant half-heartedly swore after account (7)

indicators.note: with half the heart missing: the heart of CUSSED is SS, and one S goes
one thing after another is behind it, so CUSED follows AC

blocks.note: CUSSED with one of its middle S's gone

annotation.surface: A defendant mutters oaths without conviction after giving evidence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Account' sounds like testimony in court, but it is the banking abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal usage: the accused is the person charged in a trial, the defendant.

entries.clue: Fuss following prison tweets? (8)

indicators.note: what follows comes behind, so SONG goes after BIRD

blocks.note: as in making a song and dance

annotation.surface: An outcry over tweets sent from jail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tweets' looks like social media posts, but it is birds singing. 'Doing bird' is British slang for serving time.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: tweets are the chirps birds make, one kind of birdsong.

entries.clue: Folding paper inside of comic, drinking port (7)

indicators.note: the inside of a word is everything but its outer letters
one who drinks takes something in, so OMI takes in RIGA

annotation.surface: A comedian sips port while making paper models.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Port' is the harbour city, not the wine the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: origami is the Japanese art of folding paper.

entries.clue: Restorative plant partly regressing GascoiIGNE’S NIGgle (7)

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used
to regress is to go back, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: letters inside Gascoigne's niggle, read backwards

annotation.surface: A footballer's injury worry needs a herbal tonic.
annotation.walkthrough: Paul Gascoigne was an England footballer plagued by injuries; a niggle is a minor injury. The capitals mark the hidden letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by use: ginseng root is taken as a tonic, so it is a restorative plant.

entries.clue: Time perfect exercises before international in Far East capital (6)

indicators.note: what comes before stands in front, so PE precedes I

annotation.surface: An athlete times a perfect workout before an international fixture out east.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class; the numeral 1 stands in for the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: Taipei is the capital of Taiwan, a city in the Far East.

entries.clue: Mark’s hair recedes at the front (9)

indicators.note: the receding comes at the front of the answer, so BACKS precedes LASH

annotation.surface: A man called Mark has a receding hairline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mark' is a name in the surface but the definition is a typographic mark; the 's means 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the backslash is a printed mark, the slanting stroke used in computing.

entries.clue: Gesture, very pronounced kind of wave (1-4)

indicators.note: a word pronounced is said out loud, so the wave's name is taken by its sound

annotation.surface: A very pronounced wave of the hand as a gesture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' reads as 'marked' next to 'very', but it signals a sound-alike. A V-sign made palm inwards is a rude British gesture.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a V-sign, two fingers raised in a V, is a hand gesture.

entries.clue: On reflection, whATS ARguably repressing religious type (5)

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is reversed, so the letters read backwards
to repress is to hold down inside, so the answer is held within the words

blocks.note: letters inside whats arguably, read backwards

annotation.surface: A thoughtful question about what is arguably holding a religious believer back.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals mark the hidden letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Short form: a Rasta is a Rastafarian, follower of a religious movement from Jamaica.

entries.clue: Stock cut back, say, at noon (9)

indicators.note: going back means going in reverse, so EG AT N runs backwards

annotation.surface: A shopkeeper cut back supplies at midday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut back' looks like one phrase meaning reduce, but 'cut' is PARE and 'back' reverses the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stock means ancestry or descent, which is parentage.

entries.clue: Wade’s initial shot popular with grand attendants of Queen’s (6-2-7)

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled
one thing with another is added next to it, so IN and G follow the anagram

annotation.surface: Virginia Wade's first serve at Queen's, a London tennis club, wins over the grand spectators.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initial' seems to ask for Wade's first letter, but the whole word is fodder. Virginia Wade was a British tennis champion.
annotation.definitionFit: Royal usage: ladies-in-waiting are the noblewomen who attend a queen.
